subtitle: How a dry red plateau learned to flow like a river

panels.shot: wide, low-angle view across the sun-baked Bidar plateau with distant fort walls and scattered karez shafts
panels.action: Ahmad Shah I stands on the edge of the rocky Bidar plateau, robes stirring in the hot wind, while behind him engineers peer down a dark vertical shaft that pierces the laterite like a wound of stone.

dialogue.text: On a burning red plateau where streams vanished in stone, Ahmad Shah of Bidar asked for a miracle: water that flowed uphill without a bucket or a beast.

i18n.hi: जलती लाल पट्टी पर जहाँ धाराएँ पत्थर में गुम हो जाती थीं, बेदार के अहमद शाह ने करिश्मा माँगा – पानी जो बिना डोल, बिना जानवर, ऊपर की ओर चढ़े।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view over the Deccan, showing the shift of the Bahmani court from Gulbarga to Bidar
panels.action: A sweeping map-like vista shows the old city of Gulbarga fading into the distance as a caravan of riders and carts moves toward the high ridge of Bidar under a harsh sun.

dialogue.text: In 1429, the Bahmani court left Gulbarga’s plains for Bidar’s height, chasing cooler air, stronger walls and a place to rule the Deccan from a stone crown.

i18n.hi: १४२९ में बहमनी दरबार ने गुलबर्गा के मैदानी किले से उठकर बेदार की ऊँचाई ली – ठंडी हवा, मजबूत दीवारें और दक्खन पर पत्थर का ताज पहनकर राज करने की जगह।

panels.shot: medium shot of Ahmad Shah I and courtiers on the edge of the plateau, looking down toward the plains
panels.action: Ahmad Shah I stands with advisors on a rocky escarpment, gazing over the drop to distant fields and tanks shimmering below, while near them a shallow well sits almost dry.

dialogue.text: The ridge gave him a fortress. It did not give him water. Tanks lay in the lowlands; the capital rose above them, on thirsty laterite.

i18n.hi: पहाड़ी ने उसे किला दिया, पानी नहीं। टांके नीचे के मैदानी हिस्से में थे, राजधानी ऊपर सूखी लैटराइट चट्टान पर प्यास से जूझती थी।

panels.shot: intimate mid-close shot of Ahmad Shah I in council with engineers and officials indoors
panels.action: Inside a shaded hall, Ahmad Shah I listens intently as robed engineers sketch lines and slopes on a sand-covered floor, the torchlight catching their serious faces.

dialogue.text: The chronicles do not name them, but men of craft came to his side—engineers who had seen Persia’s qanats and India’s tanks and knew what stone could hide.

i18n.hi: इतिहास नाम नहीं बताता, पर हुनरमंद लोग उसके पास आए – इंजीनियर जिन्होंने ईरान के क़नात, हिंद के टांके देखे थे और जानते थे पत्थर के भीतर क्या छुपाया जा सकता है।

panels.shot: overhead close-up of hands drawing in sand, juxtaposed with a side view of Persian hills and qanat tunnels in a ghosted overlay
panels.action: Rough hands trace a winding line with tiny cross-cuts in the sand, while faint in the background appear ghostly images of Persian hills with dotted shafts marching toward an oasis.

dialogue.text: In Iran they called it qanat, in the Deccan it would be karez—a hidden channel, dug by hand and guided by gravity, that made desert slopes run like rivers underground.

i18n.hi: ईरान में इसे क़नात कहते थे, दक्खन में बना कैरेज़ – ज़मीन के नीचे छुपी नाली, हाथ से खोदी, गुरुत्व से चलती, जो सूनी ढलानों को भीतर ही भीतर नदी बना देती।

panels.shot: medium shot at the plateau edge where engineers survey the land with simple instruments
panels.action: On the Naubad side of Bidar, engineers stand with plumb lines and water-filled bowls, sighting along the ridge as labourers look on, the red earth cracked underfoot.

dialogue.text: But Bidar was no Persian slope. It was a table of hard laterite. To bend it to their will, the engineers first had to listen to its fall and rise with rope, water and eye.

i18n.hi: पर बेदार कोई फारसी ढलान नहीं था, ये तो ठोस लैटराइट की मेज़ थी। इसे मोड़ने से पहले इंजीनियरों को रस्सी, पानी और आँख से इसकी ढलान-चढ़ान सुननी पड़ी।

panels.shot: long shot along a line of marked points stretching from lowland intake toward the plateau
panels.action: A line of stakes runs from a low-lying field toward the rising land, with men marking each point; in the foreground an engineer notes a gentle slope on a wax tablet.

dialogue.text: Step by measured step they walked a slope so slight it could not be seen, plotting a fall of only a handful of cubits over two long kilometres.

i18n.hi: कदम दर कदम वे इतनी हल्की ढलान पर चले कि आँख से दिखती ही नहीं थी, बस दो लंबे किलोमीटर में मुट्ठी भर इंचों की गिरावट नापते गए।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle shot of the first shaft being sunk, with men on ropes descending into darkness
panels.action: Workers stand in a rough circle, hauling baskets of earth from a deepening shaft, while one man clings to a rope and disappears into a dark vertical tunnel.

dialogue.text: Then they began to pierce the plateau—vertical shafts carved straight down, each a mouth into darkness, twenty-one throats for a buried stream.

i18n.hi: फिर उन्होंने पठार को छेदना शुरू किया – सीधे नीचे जाते खड़े कुएँ, हर एक अँधेरे का मुँह, ज़मीन के भीतर बहने वाली धारा के इक्कीस गले।

panels.shot: tight interior shot inside the tunnel, with two workers carving a horizontal gallery by lamplight
panels.action: By the glow of an oil lamp, bare-backed diggers chip at the laterite wall, a low horizontal tunnel stretching behind them toward another shaft where faint daylight filters in.

dialogue.text: From shaft to shaft they drove a low tunnel, no taller than a man crouched, forcing a level path through red rock so the water would never race nor stall.

i18n.hi: कुएँ से कुएँ तक उन्होंने झुके आदमी जितनी ऊँचाई का सुरंग ठोंकी, लाल पत्थर में एक सम रास्ता बनाया ताकि पानी न तेज भागे, न कहीं थमे।

panels.shot: close-up of Ahmad Shah I peering down a shaft, light from below reflecting in his eyes
panels.action: Ahmad Shah I kneels at the rim of a shaft, his face lined with concentration as a faint cool draft rises from the black below, stirring the fringe of his turban.

dialogue.text: To the king, the karez was more than a work—it was a wager. If the level was wrong by even a handspan, the capital would thirst and the effort would be buried with the tunnel.

i18n.hi: बादशाह के लिए कैरेज़ सिर्फ काम नहीं, दाँव था। स्तर एक हथेली भी चूक गया तो राजधानी प्यास से जलेगी और सारी मेहनत सुरंग के साथ दफन हो जाएगी।

panels.shot: interior tunnel shot showing the moment water breaks through into the channel
panels.action: Inside the tunnel, a worker swings his pick into a thin layer of earth; a dark trickle seeps through, then a clearer flow begins to run along the channel floor toward the cityward end.

dialogue.text: Somewhere beneath Naubad, the pick struck damp. First a stain, then a trickle, then a patient, steady run that did what no animal and no wheel could do—it climbed, unseen, toward Bidar.

i18n.hi: कहीं नौबाद के नीचे कुदाल नम मिट्टी से टकराई – पहले धब्बा, फिर बूंद, फिर धीमी पर डटी धार, जिसने जानवरों और पहियों से आगे बढ़कर काम किया – वो चुपचाप बेदार की ओर चढ़ी।

panels.shot: medium shot near a later shaft where workers test the flow with a small clay bowl
panels.action: At a shaft nearer the city, a worker kneels to scoop water from a shallow channel into a clay bowl, his face breaking into a quiet, disbelieving smile.

dialogue.text: Shaft by shaft they tested it. The flow was gentle, continuous, shielded from sun and dust. No leather buckets creaked, no oxen trudged; only earth and fall did the lifting.

i18n.hi: कुएँ-कुएँ पर उन्होंने उसे परखा – धारा नरम, लगातार, धूप और धूल से ढकी। न चमड़े की बाल्टियाँ चीखी, न बैल घिसटते; बस मिट्टी और ढलान ने सारा बोझ उठाया।

panels.shot: wide shot of Bidar’s inner precinct with a karez outlet feeding a cistern or tank
panels.action: Within the fortified city, clear water spills from a stone mouth into a stepped cistern, women filling jars and soldiers watering horses under the shadow of high ramparts.

dialogue.text: At last the hidden channel met daylight. In the heart of Bidar, a simple outlet filled a cistern, turning the laterite crown into a place where wells never ran dry in the heat.

i18n.hi: आखिर वह छुपी नाली उजाला छू गई। बेदार के दिल में एक सादा निकास ने हौज़ भर दिया, सूखी लैटराइट चोटी को ऐसा शहर बना दिया जहाँ गर्मी में कुएँ सूखते नहीं थे।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Ahmad Shah I walking along the fort walls at dusk, city life below
panels.action: Ahmad Shah I walks the parapet at dusk, looking down on lit courtyards where lamps glow beside water channels, the hum of a settled capital drifting up to him.

dialogue.text: Water did what walls alone could not. It let Bidar breathe as a capital—mosques, markets, palaces and gardens rooted in a flow that did not show itself on the surface.

i18n.hi: पानी ने वो किया जो दीवारें अकेले नहीं कर सकती थीं। उसने बेदार को राजधानी की साँस दी – मस्जिदें, बाज़ार, महल, बाग़ – सब उस बहाव पर टिका जो ऊपर से दिखता ही नहीं था।

panels.shot: documentary-style montage: cross-fade from historical karez shafts to modern ruined or blocked shafts near Bidar
panels.action: A series of images shows old masonry-lined shafts in open land fading into present-day shafts choked with debris or sealed under new construction, modern houses crowding around them.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, Yazdani would count twenty-one shafts across nearly two kilometres. Today many lie broken or buried, their lines guessed from scars on the land and memories of flow.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद यज़दानी ने लगभग दो किलोमीटर में बिखरे इक्कीस कुएँ गिने। आज कई टूटे, दबे पड़े हैं; उनकी लकीरें ज़मीन के घावों और बहाव की यादों से ही पढ़ी जाती हैं।

panels.shot: modern aerial shot suggestion, looking down on Bidar and Naubad alignment with faint traced line of the karez
panels.action: From high above, the dense fabric of modern Bidar and Naubad spreads across the plateau, a faint, imagined line tracing the old karez route beneath streets and courtyards.

dialogue.text: No full excavation has yet laid it bare. Archaeologists and conservators piece it together from shafts, alignments and the way later builders bent to its buried course.

i18n.hi: अभी तक कोई खुदाई इसे पूरा नंगा नहीं कर पाई। पुरातत्वविद और संरक्षक सिर्फ कुओं, रेखाओं और बाद के इमारती मोड़ों से इसका छुपा रास्ता जोड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on a modern conservation worker or archaeologist standing by a shaft, hand on the old masonry
panels.action: A present-day conservator stands beside a surviving shaft lined with old stone, fingertips resting on the weathered masonry as traffic and buildings loom in the background.

dialogue.text: UNESCO calls the Bidar karez significant and fragile, a thread of knowledge stretched tight between past and present, threatened by the very city it once sustained.

i18n.hi: यूनेस्को बेदार के कैरेज़ को अहम और नाज़ुक कहता है – ज्ञान की पतली डोरी, जो अतीत और आज के बीच तनी है और उसी शहर से खतरे में है जिसे कभी उसने जिंदा रखा।

panels.shot: poetic interior shot in a dark tunnel, a faint line of light from a distant shaft above
panels.action: Deep underground, the tunnel roof arches low above a dry or trickling channel, a distant shaft casting a narrow beam of daylight into the dust-choked air.

dialogue.text: We do not know every hand that dug here, nor every year the water ran. But in this quiet tunnel, stone still remembers that once, men taught it to carry a river.

i18n.hi: हम नहीं जानते किस-किस ने यहाँ फावड़ा चलाया, न ये कि पानी हर साल कितना बहा। पर इस खामोश सुरंग में पत्थर आज भी याद रखता है कि कभी इंसानों ने इसे नदी ढोना सिखाया था।

panels.shot: final wide shot blending past and present Bidar on the same plateau, hinting at continuity
panels.action: The Bidar ridge stretches under a vast sky, the old fort and modern town sharing the plateau, while in the foreground an open shaft drops into shadow, suggesting the unseen channel below.

dialogue.text: On this dry red crown of the Deccan, Ahmad Shah’s age proved a simple truth: empires fade, but when engineers read the land and trust gravity, they turn rock itself into possibility.

i18n.hi: दक्खन की इस सूखी लाल चोटी पर, अहमद शाह का ज़माना एक सीधी बात साबित कर गया – सल्तनतें मिटती हैं, पर जो इंजीनियर ज़मीन पढ़ लें और गुरुत्व पर भरोसा करें, वे पत्थर को भी संभावना में बदल देते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a dry red plateau learned to flow like a river
subtitle_i18n.hi: सूखी लाल धरती ने बहना सीखा, नदी की तरह
